profile_name: WTF Anime / Psychological, Powered and Dark
mission: Find anime built on out-thinking, hidden truth and escalating capability: psychological strategy and cat-and-mouse, mysteries that keep paying out, deep power systems and visible progression, supernatural and strange worlds - and, unlike every other profile here, horror, gore and brutality as WANTED properties rather than costs.

automation_rules.past_24h_definition: Only items with added_by=daily-automation and added_at within the last 24 hours. Bootstrap items carry added_by=bootstrap and therefore never appear in this row.
automation_rules.identity_policy: IMDb is the ONE canonical public identity and every public item must carry a real tt id. A Kitsu id may be recorded in external_ids as inert metadata for later work; it never becomes an identity, never affects dedupe, routing, posters or scoring, and can never stand in for a missing IMDb id. A candidate with no reliably resolvable IMDb id is logged as unresolved_identity and skipped for that run - it is NOT a taste rejection.
automation_rules.match_score_definition: match_score IS the deterministic baseline DNA score: the dna-match row score, post-archetype-bonus, post-guardrail, clamped 0..100. It is COMPUTED, never an invented holistic judgement. The thresholds are on that same scale and were calibrated against THIS profile's own distribution. They are NOT comparable to Fantasy 65/80, Action 60/70 or Sci-Fi 82/90.

principles.descriptive_only: A DNA value describes how strongly a property exists in a TITLE. It never states whether that property is desirable. Desirability lives only in dna_baseline and dna_guardrails - which matters unusually much here, because horror, gore and brutality are POSITIVE in this profile and negative in Sci-Fi.
principles.unknown_is_not_zero: Missing or null means UNKNOWN, never 'definitely absent'. Never substitute 0.
principles.unknown_never_satisfies: A threshold comparison against an unknown value is false in both directions. Unknown can never satisfy a positive or a negative test.
principles.unknown_is_not_safe: Unknown must not be read as 'passes the guardrail'. An item is not DNA-score-eligible unless every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails is known.
principles.independent_dimensions: Four clusters must never be merged. TONE: dark_tone (how grim the register is) is NOT horror (how much fear is the operating mode) is NOT gore (graphic bodily violence) is NOT brutality (cruelty and irreversible consequence) - a series can be deeply dark with almost no horror or gore, which is exactly the psychological-thriller shape. POWER: power_progression (the cast measurably grows) is NOT power_escalation (the setting's ceiling rises) is NOT training_growth (training depicted as process) is NOT overpowered_protagonist (the lead simply outclasses everyone) - a gag-superhero series can be low progression, low escalation, low training and maximum overpowered at once. VISUAL: visual_quality (craft) is NOT visual_uniqueness (distinctiveness) is NOT retro_visual_style (era aesthetic) - a landmark film can be high on all three, and RELEASE YEAR IS NEVER AN INPUT to any of them. ACTION: action_density (share of runtime) is NOT action_intensity (force when it occurs), and density must come from whole-runtime or season-structure evidence, never from a trailer, opening sequence or AMV.

dna_baseline.description: The desired CONTENT universe expressed on the DNA scale. Stable baseline. Accumulated user feedback is NEVER merged into this section.
dna_baseline.scale_note: Weights are -40..40 and commensurate only within this profile. horror +12 and gore +12 are the single most important cross-profile independence statement in the whole system: the Sci-Fi profile weights horror at -6 and guards against it, and Anime must never inherit that. A shared dimension id carries no shared weight.
dna_baseline.unweighted_note: pace_speed measures tempo and is used only in combination. superhero is handled entirely by a contextual combination guardrail and is left unweighted so a descriptive measurement is never confused with a policy decision - the profile has NO hard exclusions at all. weights and unweighted are disjoint and their union is exactly the 42 registry ids.

completeness_defaults.note: An item must satisfy ALL THREE conditions to be DNA-score-eligible. required_known_dimensions contains every dimension referenced anywhere in dna_guardrails. NOTE that min_known_dimensions is NOT the binding constraint for the DNA Match row: requiredFor() independently demands every weighted dimension, so a title reaching DNA Match needs all 40 weighted values. This is the most expensive profile in the system to research. Lowering min_known_dimensions would relieve nothing that binds and would only weaken the eligibility floor - research fewer titles instead.

dna_baseline.archetype_note: Best-matching archetype only, never an average. Note that the gore_horror_brutality archetype EMPHASISES the properties every other profile in this system treats as costs; that inversion is the point. Every emphasis and penalise dimension is weighted or required-known.

dna_guardrails.description: Policy applied to descriptive DNA measurements. Not learnable away by ordinary feedback.
dna_guardrails.structural_note: Judge superhero by story identity - costumed or superpowered hero-versus-villain framing - not by the mere presence of extraordinary power, which describes most of this profile's favourites.
dna_guardrails.evaluation_note: A condition whose dimension is unknown/null evaluates FALSE. This profile has NO hard exclusions: nothing is structurally banned, and every negative context is handled by weights and contextual combination penalties.

combination.note: Straight costumed hero-versus-villain framing with nothing else going on. Deliberately needs ALL FIVE conditions, because the liked exception - an absurd, massively overpowered gag take on the form - fails at least two of them and must survive. A blanket superhero ban would make that exception unrepresentable.
A relationship drama in anime clothing. Either element alone is tolerated.
Sport as the organising subject. Note this is the one negative that fires on a single dimension - the stated aversion is broad.
Piloted machines inside a military structure - the specific combination that is disliked.
Deliberately contextual: mecha carried by a strong science-fiction concept survives this, which is how a title whose ideas outweigh its mecha framing stays eligible.
Gentle everyday comedy. Absurd or transgressive comedy is a POSITIVE here and is explicitly excluded from this rule by the wtf_comedy condition.

CRAFT and DISTINCTIVENESS, not age. retro_visual_style is deliberately absent from every guardrail in this profile: an old-school look softens ranking only through its linear weight and must never exclude.

not_expressible_in_dna.consumer_rule: NO CONSUMER MAY READ, EVALUATE OR SCORE THIS FIELD. It carries zero runtime semantics.

entries.signal: Horror, gore, brutality and dark tone as negatives
entries.reason: Explicitly INVERTED in this profile. They are wanted properties carrying positive weight, and no guardrail may reference them. The Sci-Fi profile's horror aversion must never be inherited here - this is the primary cross-profile independence requirement in the system.

entries.signal: Release year / age of the title
entries.reason: Never a preference. The real objection is presentation style, measured directly by retro_visual_style, which is weight-only.
Recorded in external_ids as inert metadata only. IMDb is the one canonical public identity; a secondary id never becomes one.

execution_preferences.description: Baseline POLICY for how execution evidence would be applied if personalization were enabled. Policy only, and INERT in MG-5: this profile consumes no private feedback and generates no personalized-scores.json.
rules: Personalization is DISABLED for this profile until the cross-profile feedback v3 schema is frozen.
When enabled, a feedback event may be consumed only if its imdb_id is already in THIS repository's own public identity set.
Sci-Fi tone aspects must never be projected here: a horror thumbs-down in another profile says nothing about this one.
Execution feedback never changes topic or DNA eligibility.
Concept feedback may refine content preference, conservatively and preferably on repeated independent evidence.
A single title never establishes a generalised content aversion.
The stable baseline remains dominant while feedback history is small.

baseline_evidence.description: Audit trail for how the weights above were derived. NOT read at runtime: the weights, archetypes and guardrails ARE the encoding of this evidence. EVERY ENTRY IS UNWATCHED. Under the explicit-watch rule, watched status requires confirmation the user actually watched the title, and no such confirmation exists for any anime in the project record - only a handoff heading calling them watched anchors, which is precisely the label that proved wrong for John Wick. All of these therefore remain fully discoverable so the user can watch and rate them, and any can be promoted to watched in one edit once confirmed.
